neighbours.label: ' at' that opens 'at the time' after a past-tense clause (looking back to then)
fire: My father was teaching in Ohio at the time of the flood.
Nobody thought the decision was wrong at the time.
He was only nineteen at the time and had no money.
The road was still unpaved at the time, so we walked.
I agreed with her at the time, though I regret it now.
The band was barely known at the time of that concert.
We lived in a tiny flat at the time and shared a bed.
The law was considered fair at the time it was passed.
quiet: My father was teaching in Ohio at a small public school.
Nobody stared at the painting for very long.
He was only nineteen when he arrived at the port.
The road was still unpaved near the farm, so we walked.
I agreed with her plan and waved at the bus driver.
The band played at the stadium in front of thousands.
We lived in a tiny flat at the end of the street.
The law was passed by parliament in a late vote.
